the study of nuclear structure in the sd shell region, where the neutron and proton single particle levels are very close to each other, and with the study of the reaction mechanisms in the sd shell.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have measured lifetimes of all states in21Ne which have been previously observed in (d,p) reactions.

the lifetimes of the states at 2.68, 2.80 and 3.02 MeV are consistent with the shell model predictions, while the lifetimes of states at 2 MeV and 4.68 MeV are consistent only with the rotational model.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the DSA technique can be successfully employed to measure lifetimes of short lived states in light nuclei.

the shell model, with an appropriate choice of the effective interaction, can account for the lifetimes of the states in the low-lying part of the spectrum, but fails for the higher excited states, which are best described by a rotational model.
